1. **Deconvolution:** run multideconv on both cohorts with the same methods and signatures.
2. **Training on Gide** (73 samples; R = positive class): pipeML with `fold_construction_fun="prepare_multideconv_folds"`. This rebuilds the cross-method cell-type subgroups inside each training fold, so the cross-validation estimate stays leakage-free. It uses repeated stratified k-fold CV.
3. **External test on Riaz** (51 samples): project Riaz onto Gide's final subgroups with `replicate_subgroups`, then score it with `predict_ml_model` (AUROC/AUPRC). Riaz has only 10 responders, so its estimate will be noisy.
4. **Feature drivers:** SHAP values on the final model, plus a summary of which cell-type features push predictions toward response.

Everything will be saved under `results/`.

field_glossary.Discarded features with high number of z: Features dropped for exceeding zero_thr fraction of samples at zero -- usually a cell type this cohort's data can't reliably distinguish from absent.
field_glossary.Discarded features with low variance: Features dropped for near-constant values across samples (coefficient of variation, sd/mean, below cv_thr) -- uninformative for distinguishing samples from each other.

# Summarize test-set performance and SHAP feature drivers of the Gide-trained TME model.
suppressMessages(library(ggplot2))
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
res <- if (length(args)) args[1] else "results"
out <- file.path(res, "06_feature_drivers_summary")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- External test performance (Riaz)
pred <- readRDS(file.path(res, "04_external_test_Riaz/prediction/result.rds"))
auc <- pred$AUC
capture.output(str(auc), file = file.path(out, "Riaz_test_AUC.txt"))
print(auc)

# Riaz predictions also stratified by observed response
cl <- read.csv(file.path(res, "inputs/Riaz_clinical.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
p <- pred$Predictions
p$sample <- rownames(p); p$Response <- cl$Response[match(p$sample, cl$sample)]
write.csv(p, file.path(out, "Riaz_predictions_with_response.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(wilcox.test(yes ~ Response, data = p))

# --- SHAP global importance and direction
shap <- read.csv(file.path(res, "05_SHAP_feature_importance/result.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
model <- readRDS(file.path(res, "03_model_training_Gide/result.rds"))
X <- model$Model$trainingData
X <- X[, colnames(shap), drop = FALSE]
y <- model$Model$trainingData$.outcome

imp <- data.frame(
  feature = colnames(shap),
  mean_abs_SHAP = colMeans(abs(shap)),
  # Direction: Spearman correlation between a feature's value and its SHAP value
  # (> 0: higher abundance pushes the prediction toward response)
  direction_rho = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) suppressWarnings(cor(X[[f]], shap[[f]], method = "spearman"))),
  median_in_R = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) median(X[[f]][y == "yes"])),
  median_in_NR = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) median(X[[f]][y == "no"])),
  wilcox_p_R_vs_NR = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(X[[f]] ~ y)$p.value))
)
imp$effect <- ifelse(imp$direction_rho > 0, "higher -> Response", "higher -> Non-response")
imp$cell_type <- sub("_Subgroup\\..*$", "", sub("^[^_]+_[^_]+_", "", imp$feature))
imp <- imp[order(-imp$mean_abs_SHAP), ]
imp$rank <- seq_len(nrow(imp))

# Subgroup composition: which method/signature features each subgroup merges
comp <- model$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
members <- unlist(lapply(comp, function(ct) {
  if (is.null(ct) || !length(ct)) return(NULL)
  sapply(ct, function(m) paste(m, collapse = "; "))
}))
names(members) <- sub("^[^.]*\\.(.*_Subgroup\\.\\d+)$", "\\1", names(members))
imp$subgroup_members <- ifelse(imp$feature %in% names(members), members[imp$feature], "")
write.csv(imp, file.path(out, "SHAP_feature_importance_ranked.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Aggregate importance per cell type
ct <- aggregate(mean_abs_SHAP ~ cell_type, imp, sum)
ct <- ct[order(-ct$mean_abs_SHAP), ]
write.csv(ct, file.path(out, "SHAP_importance_per_cell_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

print(head(imp[, c("rank", "feature", "mean_abs_SHAP", "direction_rho", "effect", "wilcox_p_R_vs_NR")], 25), row.names = FALSE)
print(head(ct, 15), row.names = FALSE)

# --- Plots
top <- head(imp, 20)
top$feature <- factor(top$feature, levels = rev(top$feature))
g1 <- ggplot(top, aes(mean_abs_SHAP, feature, fill = effect)) + geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("higher -> Response" = "#2b8cbe", "higher -> Non-response" = "#e34a33")) +
  labs(x = "mean |SHAP| (probability of response)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Top 20 TME features driving response prediction (RF, Gide)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_top20_importance.pdf"), g1, width = 9, height = 7)

long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(as.character(top$feature), function(f)
  data.frame(feature = f, shap = shap[[f]], value = rank(X[[f]]) / nrow(X))))
long$feature <- factor(long$feature, levels = levels(top$feature))
g2 <- ggplot(long, aes(shap, feature, colour = value)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#3182bd", high = "#de2d26", name = "Feature value\n(rank, low->high)") +
  labs(x = "SHAP value (impact on P(response))", y = NULL, title = "SHAP beeswarm, top 20 features") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_top20_beeswarm.pdf"), g2, width = 10, height = 7)

ctp <- head(ct, 15); ctp$cell_type <- factor(ctp$cell_type, levels = rev(ctp$cell_type))
g3 <- ggplot(ctp, aes(mean_abs_SHAP, cell_type)) + geom_col(fill = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "summed mean |SHAP| over the cell type's features", y = NULL, title = "Importance per cell type") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_importance_per_cell_type.pdf"), g3, width = 8, height = 6)

# Summarize test-set performance and SHAP feature drivers of the Gide-trained TME model.
suppressMessages(library(ggplot2))
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
res <- if (length(args)) args[1] else "results"
out <- file.path(res, "06_feature_drivers_summary")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- External test performance (Riaz)
pred <- readRDS(file.path(res, "04_external_test_Riaz/prediction/result.rds"))
auc <- pred$AUC
capture.output(str(auc), file = file.path(out, "Riaz_test_AUC.txt"))
print(auc)

# Riaz predictions also stratified by observed response
cl <- read.csv(file.path(res, "inputs/Riaz_clinical.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
p <- pred$Predictions
p$sample <- rownames(p); p$Response <- cl$Response[match(p$sample, cl$sample)]
write.csv(p, file.path(out, "Riaz_predictions_with_response.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(wilcox.test(yes ~ Response, data = p))

# --- SHAP global importance and direction
shap <- read.csv(file.path(res, "05_SHAP_feature_importance/result.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
model <- readRDS(file.path(res, "03_model_training_Gide/result.rds"))
X <- model$Model$trainingData
X <- X[, colnames(shap), drop = FALSE]
y <- model$Model$trainingData$.outcome

imp <- data.frame(
  feature = colnames(shap),
  mean_abs_SHAP = colMeans(abs(shap)),
  # Direction: Spearman correlation between a feature's value and its SHAP value
  # (> 0: higher abundance pushes the prediction toward response)
  direction_rho = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) suppressWarnings(cor(X[[f]], shap[[f]], method = "spearman"))),
  median_in_R = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) median(X[[f]][y == "yes"])),
  median_in_NR = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) median(X[[f]][y == "no"])),
  wilcox_p_R_vs_NR = sapply(colnames(shap), function(f) suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(X[[f]] ~ y)$p.value))
)
imp$effect <- ifelse(imp$direction_rho > 0, "higher -> Response", "higher -> Non-response")
imp$cell_type <- sub("_Subgroup\\..*$", "", sub("^[^_]+_[^_]+_", "", imp$feature))
imp <- imp[order(-imp$mean_abs_SHAP), ]
imp$rank <- seq_len(nrow(imp))

# Subgroup composition: which method/signature features each subgroup merges
comp <- model$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
members <- unlist(lapply(comp, function(ct) {
  if (is.null(ct) || !length(ct)) return(NULL)
  sapply(ct, function(m) paste(m, collapse = "; "))
}))
names(members) <- sub("^[^.]*\\.(.*_Subgroup\\.\\d+)$", "\\1", names(members))
imp$subgroup_members <- ifelse(imp$feature %in% names(members), members[imp$feature], "")
write.csv(imp, file.path(out, "SHAP_feature_importance_ranked.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Aggregate importance per cell type
ct <- aggregate(mean_abs_SHAP ~ cell_type, imp, sum)
ct <- ct[order(-ct$mean_abs_SHAP), ]
write.csv(ct, file.path(out, "SHAP_importance_per_cell_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

print(head(imp[, c("rank", "feature", "mean_abs_SHAP", "direction_rho", "effect", "wilcox_p_R_vs_NR")], 25), row.names = FALSE)
print(head(ct, 15), row.names = FALSE)

# --- Plots
top <- head(imp, 20)
top$feature <- factor(top$feature, levels = rev(top$feature))
g1 <- ggplot(top, aes(mean_abs_SHAP, feature, fill = effect)) + geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("higher -> Response" = "#2b8cbe", "higher -> Non-response" = "#e34a33")) +
  labs(x = "mean |SHAP| (probability of response)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Top 20 TME features driving response prediction (RF, Gide)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_top20_importance.pdf"), g1, width = 9, height = 7)

long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(as.character(top$feature), function(f)
  data.frame(feature = f, shap = shap[[f]], value = rank(X[[f]]) / nrow(X))))
long$feature <- factor(long$feature, levels = levels(top$feature))
g2 <- ggplot(long, aes(shap, feature, colour = value)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#3182bd", high = "#de2d26", name = "Feature value\n(rank, low->high)") +
  labs(x = "SHAP value (impact on P(response))", y = NULL, title = "SHAP beeswarm, top 20 features") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_top20_beeswarm.pdf"), g2, width = 10, height = 7)

ctp <- head(ct, 15); ctp$cell_type <- factor(ctp$cell_type, levels = rev(ctp$cell_type))
g3 <- ggplot(ctp, aes(mean_abs_SHAP, cell_type)) + geom_col(fill = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "summed mean |SHAP| over the cell type's features", y = NULL, title = "Importance per cell type") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "SHAP_importance_per_cell_type.pdf"), g3, width = 8, height = 6)

I built a Random Forest that separates responders from non-responders well in leakage-free cross-validation on Gide, but it only weakly predicts response in Riaz. The CD8 T-cell and monocyte/macrophage features drive the predictions.

**Setup**
- **Input scale:** both files are log2(TPM+1). For deconvolution I converted them to linear TPM (2^x − 1) and rescaled each sample to sum to 1e6. That rescaling was needed because Gide's column sums ranged from 41k to 730k.
- **Deconvolution:** multideconv ran 5 methods (Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS, CIBERSORTx) with its built-in signatures, giving 375 cell-type estimates per sample.
- **Training:** on Gide (73 samples: 46 responders, 27 non-responders). The grouping of agreeing method estimates into cell-type subgroups was redone inside every cross-validation fold, so test samples never influenced their own features. I used 5 folds repeated 10 times and compared 11 algorithms.
- **Test:** Riaz (51 samples: 10 responders, 41 non-responders) was mapped onto the final model's subgroups and then scored.

**Performance**

| | AUROC | AUPRC |
|---|---|---|
| Gide, cross-validation (Random Forest, best of 11) | **0.81** (MAD 0.09) | 0.90 (chance level 0.63) |
| Riaz, external test | **0.61** (95% CI 0.42–0.81) | 0.26 (chance level 0.20) |

The Riaz confidence interval includes 0.5, so I can't claim the model works on an independent cohort. Likely reasons:
- Riaz has only 10 responders.
- Gide includes anti-PD1 plus anti-CTLA4 patients, while Riaz is anti-PD1 only.
- The cohorts were sequenced and processed differently.

The Gide estimate shows the composition signal is real within that cohort; it does not show that it carries over to other cohorts.

**Features driving the prediction** (SHAP values on the final model)
- **Pointing to response:**
  - CD8 T cells, both the CIBERSORTx/TIL10 estimate and the TIL10 subgroup where four methods agree. In Gide responders the median is about 0.03, versus about 0 in non-responders.
  - M1 macrophages: the LM22 subgroup (0.040 vs 0.005) and the TIL10 subgroup.
- **Pointing to non-response:**
  - Monocytes are the single strongest feature (median 0.03 in responders vs 0.13 in non-responders).
  - M2 macrophages (0.18 vs 0.27).
  - Resting mast cells, memory B cells, and the cancer-cell fraction.

Overall, a cytotoxic, M1-polarized immune environment goes with response, and a monocyte/M2-dominated or tumour-dominated one goes with non-response. This fits what is known about checkpoint-inhibitor response in melanoma. SHAP describes how the model uses features on its own training data, so these drivers come from Gide; given the weak Riaz result, I wouldn't assume they generalize.

- The first deconvolution attempt was killed for lack of memory (15 GB machine). I reran it one cohort at a time with 4 parallel workers instead of 19.

# Convert already-produced results into a standard format (no recomputation).
suppressMessages(library(jsonlite))
res <- "results"
out <- file.path(res, "standard")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

input_ids <- function(co) {
  h <- readLines(sprintf("data/%s_log2TPM.txt", co), n = 1)
  strsplit(h, "\t")[[1]][-1]
}
with_patient <- function(df, ids_expected) {
  stopifnot(setequal(rownames(df), ids_expected))
  cbind(patient = rownames(df), df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
gide_ids <- input_ids("Gide"); riaz_ids <- input_ids("Riaz")

# Raw deconvolution (Gide: copy with original IDs restored from the deconvolution step's output)
d <- read.csv(file.path(res, "inputs/Gide_deconvolution_raw.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(with_patient(d, gide_ids), file.path(out, "deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
d <- read.csv(file.path(res, "01_deconvolution/Riaz/result.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(with_patient(d, riaz_ids), file.path(out, "deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Subgroup composition of the final model (fold-construction refit on all Gide training samples)
comp <- readRDS(file.path(res, "03_model_training_Gide/final_model_subgroups.rds"))[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
rows <- do.call(rbind, unname(lapply(comp, function(ct) {
  if (is.null(ct) || !length(ct)) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ct), function(s) data.frame(subgroup = s, feature = ct[[s]])))
})))
write.csv(rows, file.path(out, "subgroups_composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# CV performance
a <- read.csv(file.path(res, "03_model_training_Gide/result_AUROC_median.csv"))
write.csv(data.frame(algorithm = a$model, cv_auroc = a$Median_AUROC), file.path(out, "cv_performance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Test predictions (Riaz)
p <- read.csv(file.path(res, "04_external_test_Riaz/prediction/result_Predictions.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(setequal(rownames(p), riaz_ids))
write.csv(data.frame(patient = rownames(p), probability_R = p$yes), file.path(out, "test_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Feature importance (mean |SHAP|)
fi <- read.csv(file.path(res, "06_feature_drivers_summary/SHAP_feature_importance_ranked.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(feature = fi$feature, cell_type = fi$cell_type, importance = fi$mean_abs_SHAP),
          file.path(out, "feature_importance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# SHAP values (Gide training samples)
s <- read.csv(file.path(res, "05_SHAP_feature_importance/result.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(with_patient(s, gide_ids), file.path(out, "shap_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Run info
info <- list(selected_algorithm = "RF", training_cohort = "Gide", test_cohort = "Riaz",
             features_built_inside_cv_folds = TRUE, cv_folds = 5, cv_repeats = 10,
             metric = "AUROC", cibersortx = TRUE)
write_json(info, file.path(out, "info.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

for (f in list.files(out, full.names = TRUE)) cat(basename(f), if (grepl("csv$", f)) paste(dim(read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)), collapse = "x"), "\n")

I wrote all 7 requested files to `results/standard/` by converting existing outputs only. Nothing was recomputed and no existing file was changed. A check confirmed that every `patient` column matches the sample names in the input expression files.

Where each file comes from:
- **`deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv`** (73 × 375 features): `results/inputs/Gide_deconvolution_raw.csv`. This is the deconvolution step's output with the original sample IDs restored (the step had added an "X" prefix).
- **`deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv`** (51 × 375): `01_deconvolution/Riaz/result.csv`.
- **`subgroups_composition.csv`** (207 member rows): the final model's subgroup definitions, learned on all Gide training samples. These are not from the descriptive full-data harmonization run.
- **`cv_performance.csv`** (11 algorithms): the median cross-validation AUROC of each algorithm.
- **`test_predictions.csv`** (51 Riaz patients): the predicted probability of response.
- **`feature_importance.csv`** (181 features): mean absolute SHAP value per feature. The `cell_type` column comes from my summary script, which parsed it out of the feature names.
- **`shap_values.csv`**: SHAP values for the 73 Gide training patients (the final model was explained on its training data) × 181 features.
- **`info.json`**: Random Forest, trained on Gide, tested on Riaz, features built inside the CV folds, 5 folds × 10 repeats, AUROC, CIBERSORTx used.

I also added one new file, `results/scripts/export_standard.R`, which does this conversion.
